Vehicles make their way through a badly damaged road at Kottar in Nagercoil.
Recent wet spells have worsened the condition of Cape Road at Kottar in Kanniyakunari district, with the potholes creating hazardous conditions for motorists using the busy State Highways stretch every day.
Kottar, a major commercial hub in the region, attracts thousands of people and goods vehicles from various parts of the State because of its wholesale grocery and retail markets. The damaged stretch also serves as an important route for daily commuters as several schools and hospitals are located along the route.
The movement of heavy goods vehicles and trucks cause damage to the roads, and the authorities must conduct regular inspection to identify and repair vulnerable stretches, says Balan, an autorickshaw driver
“The potholes pose a significant safety hazard to motorists. As the damage remains unattended, the potholes are likely to widen rapidly, particularly during the ongoing spell.” he adds.
With rainwater accumulating in the potholes and reducing their visibility, motorists face difficulties in identifying and avoiding them. Residents and road users have called for immediate repair work to prevent accidents and ensure the safe movement of vehicles along the stretch.
A trader in the area says the road has been deteriorating and a concrete solution is necessary. Even after the road was relaid with tar, portions of it have been often dug up within a few weeks for various works, resulting in further damage.
The authorities must restore the damaged stretch immediately and take measures to prevent the recurrence of potholes, which pose a threat to road users.
An official from the State Highways Department told The Hindu that the damaged area would be inspected and temporary repair work would be undertaken. The pothole-ridden road would be relaid with tar after the rain subsided.
